# Motion MCP

> Motion MCP is an open-source (MIT) motion-video production runtime exposed as a Streamable HTTP MCP server. A host model (Claude, ChatGPT, Pi or any other MCP client) calls `motion_create` with a brief and gets back a rendered, web-optimized MP4. Status: in active development; the hosted endpoint is in early access.

## Connect

- MCP endpoint: https://app.motion.digitop.ai/mcp (stateless Streamable HTTP)
- Auth: every request sends `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. Keys are per workspace and are created in the dashboard: https://app.motion.digitop.ai
- Clients must send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.
- Start with `motion_inspect({ "target": "capabilities" })`. It returns the server version, director modes, the CreativeSpec JSON Schema, prompt guidance, pricing and limits.

Example client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "motion": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://app.motion.digitop.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer mmcp_YOUR_API_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools (the full public surface)

- `motion_create`: start a video from a `brief`. Optional `directorMode`, `creativeSpec` (required for host-opus), `recipeId`, `format`, `quality` ("preview" default, or "final"), `budgetCredits`. Returns `projectId`, `jobId`, `status`, `next`.
- `motion_edit`: revise a project with an `instruction` or `scenePatches`; also answers host critique requests via `critiqueRequestId`.
- `motion_inspect`: `target` is "capabilities", "project", "scene" or "styles".
- `motion_render`: render a version at "preview" or "final" quality, as mp4 or webm. Final requires lint and check to pass.
- `motion_search`: search styles, patterns, recipes, registry blocks, projects, scenes and assets.
- `motion_get_project`: poll job state, stage and progress; optionally include versions, renders, usage and trace.
- `motion_list_projects`: paginated project list.
- `motion_publish`: publish a succeeded final render at a stable share URL (unlisted or public).

Long-running tools return a `jobId` immediately. Poll `motion_get_project` until the job is `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`. The state `awaiting_host` means the job is waiting for a host critique.

## Director modes

- `host-opus`: the calling host writes the CreativeSpec using the schema from `motion_inspect`. A valid spec skips the internal director and its cost; an invalid spec returns validation issues with no Opus spend. Use when the host is already a frontier model.
- `internal-opus`: Motion MCP calls Opus through OpenRouter for creative direction. Use when the host is a small model or a script.
- The server never infers the mode from model names; pass `directorMode` or rely on the workspace default.

## How it works

Opus is the creative director (spec and critique only; it never writes HyperFrames HTML). Jev, a bounded decision model, routes work with typed, traced decisions. A deterministic compiler builds scenes from Motion IR; Pi driving a cheap coder model handles scenes that need bespoke code. HyperFrames lints, checks, snapshots and renders in a pinned Linux container, and FFmpeg finishes the MP4.

## Cost

- 1 credit = US$0.01. Prices are early access and indicative; live values come from `motion_inspect` capabilities.
- Frontier tokens are spent only on taste: creative direction and critique. Everything mechanical is code.
- `budgetCredits` caps a job. A job whose estimated cost exceeds its remaining budget stops and reports the shortfall.
